title: Field Journal: SIEM Export and Audit Handoff
content:
Purpose
-----
Quick working notes for handoff of collected audit exports to the analysis team and for use by on-call engineers during live security events. Not an official playbook — this is a field journal with pragmatic mappings, export patterns, and short checklists we can run with when time is tight.

Scope and why this exists
------------------------
- Problem: during incidents we scramble to produce an ingestion-friendly SIEM payload that keeps RBAC context (role deltas, policy id, requester) and evidence hashes.
- Goal: standardize the minimum useful export (JSONL) and an evidence handoff checklist so triage/forensics can start without asking for more basics.
- Assumes RBAC v2 is in place (role inheritance, temporary grants) and that audit logs are emitted to both central logging (stack-driver-like) and a raw S3 bucket.

Minimum export schema (opinionated)
----------------------------------
Note: audit-schema-v2 is a superset. For emergency exports prefer this compact set so SIEM ingestion is fast.
- audit_schema_version: "v2"
- timestamp: "2024-11-02T15:24:31Z"  (ISO8601 UTC)
- event_id: "uuid-v4"
- request_id: "incoming-proxy-id / lambda-exec-id"
- actor_id: "user|service-account|short-id"
- actor_email: "alice@example.com"
- actor_roles: "[admin, billing-reader]"  (stringified list allowed)
- action: "grant_role | revoke_role | api_call | login | token_create"
- resource: "/projects/prod/model-card/123"
- resource_type: "model|project|secret|route"
- outcome: "success | failure | partial"
- ip: "203.0.113.52"
- user_agent: "curl/7.85"
- geo: "US-CA"
- before_roles: "[reader]"  (present for role-change events)
- after_roles: "[reader, admin]"  (present for role-change events)
- policy_id: "rbac-v2-policy-42"  (if applicable)
- retention_bucket_path: "s3://redwood-audit-raw/2024/11/02/"  (where full raw event stored)
- evidence_blob: "s3://redwood-forensics/incident-2024-11-02/ev-1.gz"  (optional pointer)

Formatting notes for export
---------------------------
- Single-line JSON (JSONL): one event per line. Name file with incident tag + sequence: redwood-export-20241102-incident-93-0001.jsonl.gz
- Compress with gzip (level 6) before transfer to Splunk HEC or Elastic ingest. If going direct to Splunk HTTP Event Collector, send in batches of 500 events or 5MB whichever comes first.
- For Elastic, prefer bulk API with action/meta + document pairs. Mapper: use the compact schema as the _source document; put event_id as _id.
- Timestamp must be parsed by ingest pipeline as @timestamp (ISO format).

RBAC v2 specifics to preserve in exports
---------------------------------------
- Temporary grants: include grant_expiry when actor_roles includes ephemeral roles. Without expiry triage may misattribute escalation windows.
- Inheritance flattening: export both raw role tokens and a flattened effective_roles array so investigations don't need to re-evaluate policy graph.
- Service account chain: capture parent_service_account_id for chained impersonation.
- Admin override/justification: if an action uses emergency override, include override_ticket_id and justification text (even if short).

Evidence preservation checklist (for on-call)
--------------------------------------------
- Step 1: snapshot the raw logging stream window (T0-15m to T0+15m) to S3 path: s3://redwood-incident-archive/<incident-id>/raw-logs/
- Step 2: export current RBAC policy dump (rbac-v2-policy-YYYYMMDD.json) to same incident path.
- Step 3: take a read-only snapshot of affected DB tables (access-control, tokens). If DB snapshot not possible, export CSV of rows (sha256 hashed ids) to forensic folder.
- Step 4: capture running node process list and network connections for involved hosts (if on-prem) and store compressed; include hostnames and boot IDs.
- Step 5: calculate SHA256 on each artifact and record hashes in a manifest (manifest.txt).
- Step 6: lock down the S3 path with a short-term KMS policy to prevent accidental deletion. Notify infra-owner.

Quick incident flow for first-on-call (short, actionable)
---------------------------------------------------------
1) Rapid intake: create incident ticket (template: SEC-QuickStart) and assign incident-id. Post alert in #sec-ops with incident-id and short summary.
2) Contain: if the alert indicates active token compromise, revoke tokens scoped to the vector (do not mass revoke org tokens without approval). Use service 'token-revoke --filter request_id' tool.
3) Export minimal SIEM JSONL (see schema) for T0-30m window and upload to incident S3 path.
4) Snapshot RBAC policy + role-grants for actors. Add to incident S3 path.
5) Escalate to forensics within 30 minutes if evidence indicates data exfiltration or credential exposure.
6) Keep Slack thread pinned; update ticket with steps taken and link to S3 artifacts.

Automation hooks (ideas + existing connectors)
--------------------------------------------
- Connector: Splunk HEC + prefix filter. Issue: HEC rate limits; fallback to S3 sink when HEC refused.
- Lambda job: auto-collect logs for flagged request_id, produce JSONL, push to s3://redwood-incident-automation/<incident-id>/ and notify #sec-ops with presigned URL.
- K8s sidecar: when an agent detects anomaly in audit stream, it writes local evidence bundle and triggers a CRD that starts the collection job.
- PagerDuty integration: on critical export success/fail, send actionable note (what file path, who to call).

Edge cases we keep hitting (open TODOs)
-------------------------------------
- Time skew: some services still emit local timestamps. Need to standardize on ingest to convert to UTC and flag events with >5s skew. TODO: add metric.
- PII in logs: sometimes user_email shows full email; consider tokenized_email field for public incident summaries.
- Large binary blobs: model weights or snapshots can be huge — prefer a pointer + minimal metadata in audit export and keep binary retention policy separate.

Communication and handoff notes
-------------------------------
- When handing off to investigations, include: incident-id, short summary, list of artifacts (S3 paths + hashes), timeline of key events (with event_ids), and the compact JSONL used for SIEM ingest.
- If legal or compliance is involved, create a sealed folder (s3://redwood-legal-hold/<incident-id>/) and copy artifacts there; notify legal@redwood.
- Red team/third parties: do not mix red-team evidence into the same incident folder as production incidents — tag clearly.

Quick templates (snippets to drop into ticket / Slack)
-----------------------------------------------------
- Slack alert (first message): "SEC - incident-93 created. short: suspected token misuse. artifacts: s3://redwood-incident-archive/incident-93/raw-logs/ (manifest attached). On-call: @sec-oncall-now"
- Incident ticket summary (concise): "incident-93 | suspected lateral movement via temporary admin grant | initial detection 2024-11-02T15:20Z | exported SIEM compact file redwood-export-20241102-incident-93-0001.jsonl.gz"

Notes to future selves
---------------------
- This is intentionally compact. When we have time convert to formal runbook and create automated tests that validate mapping and sample exports against the ingest pipelines.
- Double-check retention policy alignment: forensics folder should match legal retention for incidents (currently 7 years for certain data classes).
- Revisit whether to include full policy diffs (git style) vs. JSON snapshots in exports — diffs are smaller but harder to parse quickly.

Unresolved questions (please contribute)
-------------------------------------
- Do we want to include full pre/post policy diffs in every role-change export or only on demand?
- Should the compact export include hashed_email or plain email? (tradeoff: investigator speed vs. exposure)
- Are we confident KMS key rotation won't block emergency artifact access? Who is emergency key custodian?

End notes / next steps
---------------------
- Marco: can you prototype the Lambda that creates the compact JSONL and uploads to incident path? (JIRA SEC-872)
- Elena: coordinate with Splunk team to test bulk ingest with 1k test events (use dev index).
- Samir: draft short policy for ephemeral role export fields (grant_expiry).

-- A.P. (field notes)
